Hi Alex – quick technical reply to address the items you listed. I can expand during the sync with your platform team.

1) Recommended pattern
- For server-to-server: we recommend using service accounts with short-lived JWTs exchanged for bearer tokens (OAuth2-like flow). Redwood supports both long-lived API keys and short-lived tokens; for production we prefer service accounts + KMS-backed signing to minimize blast radius.

2) JWKS / token issuance
- Redwood can be configured to accept your identity provider (IDP) via OIDC federation or we can issue tokens from our token service. We publish a JWKS endpoint for token verification and support standard RS256 JWTs.

3) Key rotation
- Best practice: store signing keys in customer-managed KMS (GCP KMS / AWS KMS / Azure Key Vault) when using Redwood Private. For Hosted, we offer KMS integrations. Rotation: automate key rollover monthly or on-rotation event; we support multi-key acceptance window (old key grace period) to avoid disruptions. We emit rotation events and audit logs that can be forwarded to your SIEM.

4) Embeddings & quotas
- Embedding calls use the same bearer tokens as other API endpoints. We apply per-account and per-route quotas; we can carve out separate quota buckets for embedding workloads to protect throughput.

5) SDK / service-account example
- Attaching example-service-account.json as a stub (see attachment). Minimal flow:
  a) Create service account in your platform with restricted scopes (inference:read,inference:invoke,embeddings:invoke).
  b) Use your KMS to sign a short-lived JWT (exp <= 5m).
  c) Exchange JWT with Redwood token endpoint for ephemeral bearer token.
  d) Call inference endpoint with bearer token; include x-request-id, route headers for routing to dedicated pool.

6) Structured output / function-calling
- No special auth required; function-calling is configured per-model endpoint. If you plan to use tool-calling that triggers external webhooks, we recommend using service accounts for those worker services and encrypting webhook secrets in your KMS.

I'll bring a short architecture sketch to the call.

—Dev
